what: the render half of #787: a sound-only render of an MPEG-TS or MPEG-PS still counted from the sound's own first sample after the reads were moved onto the file's clock. On a .ts, .m2ts or .mpg whose sound starts 0.28 s after its picture, cut.py --start 0.5 -o out.wav put a burst at 1.0 s at 0.72 s instead of 0.5, loudness.py and audio.py --gain 0 to .wav at 0.72 instead of 1.0, and silence.py -o out.wav (its plan on the file's clock, its cut on the sound's) at 0.0 instead of 0.2; check.py --content's dropout pass put a gap at 2.0 s at 1.71 s. MP4 and Matroska wrote and read every one right. The same class in loop.py: the concat demuxer gives an MPEG-PS's video no start_time, so concat_first_frame() fell back to 0.0 and av_trim cut the sound's 0.29 s lead off the first repeat (393 frames for 400, 15.72 s for 16 s, verified False)
escaped: #792 moved every sound-only read onto probe.sound_clock() and its guard compared the sweep rows of the reading tools; the renders were not in it, because a sweep row says what a tool reports and a .wav whose lead is missing is a completed, verified row. check.py's dropout pass is its own decode, outside detect_silences, and check.py was not among the guard's tools
mechanism: every sound-only render calls probe.sound_clock() with -copyts when the file's start time is not 0 (an MP4 or MKV that starts at 0 runs the same command as before): cut.py's audio re-encode and _join_chunk's inputs when no picture is cut, loudness.py's second pass (the trim counts the padded lead), audio.py's main track and its music and effects beds (sound_clock(pad=False) on a bed, which amix plays from the output's start on every container), and probe._detect_dropouts. test_guards.TimeGuard.test_a_sound_read_alone_counts_from_the_files_start renders cut, loudness, audio and silence to .wav and runs check.py --content on a .ts and an .mp4 of the same content whose sound starts late, and fails where the first burst or the dropout differ. loop.concat_first_frame() takes the first frame's best_effort_timestamp when the stream has no start_time; test_editing.OneClockTests.test_loop_of_an_mpeg_ps_whose_sound_starts_late_keeps_every_frame_787
